name: spawn_task
description: Start one-off work now as a subtask: in the background, or inline with await_result=true when you need the answer in this turn. For later or recurring work use schedule_task; for several steps with dependencies, waits or approvals use dag_create.

input_schema.description: Start one-off work now as a subtask: in the background, or inline with await_result=true when you need the answer in this turn. For later or recurring work use schedule_task; for several steps with dependencies, waits or approvals use dag_create.

timeout.description: Max execution seconds (clamped to server max)

frame_type.description: Cognitive frame for the subtask. If omitted, auto-detected.

await_result.description: If true, wait for subtask completion and return result inline. Default false (fire-and-forget).

model.description: Model to use for this subtask. If omitted, uses default background model. Use a smaller model for fast lookup/summarization tasks.

output_format.description: How the subtask should structure its final report. Optional; sensible default applied per frame_type.

success_criteria.description: What 'done' looks like. Optional; default 'summary directly addresses the task and is internally consistent'.

payload_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the subtask's result payload. On a mismatch the subtask retries, then ends as 'validation_failed'. A JSON object or a boolean (true accepts any payload, false rejects all).

name: schedule_task
description: Run a task later, once ('when'), or on a repeat ('every'); give exactly one. For work to start now use spawn_task; to watch for a change and report it use heartbeat_check_create.

input_schema.description: Run a task later, once ('when'), or on a repeat ('every'); give exactly one. For work to start now use spawn_task; to watch for a change and report it use heartbeat_check_create.

when.description: One-shot time: 'in 2 hours', ISO 8601, or natural language

every.description: Recurring pattern: 'daily at 8am', '30 minutes', 'every monday at 10am'

model.description: Model to use for this scheduled task. If omitted, uses default background model.

concurrency_policy.description: Recurring only: what a fire does while this schedule's previous run (its subtask, or a DAG it created) is still active. coalesce_if_active (default) and skip_if_active start nothing; always_enqueue starts another run.

catch_up_policy.description: Recurring only: slots missed while Nous was down. skip_missed (default) runs once; enqueue_missed_with_cap runs once per missed slot up to catch_up_cap (each run still passes concurrency_policy, so the extra runs only start with always_enqueue).

catch_up_cap.description: Most runs enqueue_missed_with_cap starts at once (1-25; default 3).

name: spawn_sync
description: Run a subtask synchronously (inline) and return a typed SubtaskResult containing status, structured payload, raw text, and confidence. Pass payload_schema to require the subtask's report.payload to validate against a JSON Schema; on mismatch the SubtaskResult will have status='validation_failed'. Use spawn_task for fire-and-forget.

input_schema.description: Run a subtask synchronously (inline) and return a typed SubtaskResult containing status, structured payload, raw text, and confidence. Pass payload_schema to require the subtask's report.payload to validate against a JSON Schema; on mismatch the SubtaskResult will have status='validation_failed'. Use spawn_task for fire-and-forget.

payload_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 compatible). When set, the subtask is instructed to populate submit_final_report's `payload` field with data matching this schema; the executor validates the result post-hoc. May be a JSON object or a boolean (draft 2020-12 boolean-as-schema).

frame_type.description: Cognitive frame for the subtask. Defaults to current.

timeout_seconds.description: Max execution seconds (clamped to server max).

model.description: Model to use for this subtask. Defaults to background model.

success_criteria.description: What 'done' looks like. Optional; defaults to a generic check.

name: dag_create
description: Run several steps with dependencies, waits or approvals as a DAG of nodes. Limits: 10 nodes in all, fix nodes included; 4 waves (steps in a dependency chain) and 4 nodes per wave, fix nodes not counted. Do not poll: the outcome is delivered to you when it ends. Use dag_manage to cancel, retry or check progress. For one task, use spawn_task.

input_schema.description: Run several steps with dependencies, waits or approvals as a DAG of nodes. Limits: 10 nodes in all, fix nodes included; 4 waves (steps in a dependency chain) and 4 nodes per wave, fix nodes not counted. Do not poll: the outcome is delivered to you when it ends. Use dag_manage to cancel, retry or check progress. For one task, use spawn_task.

description.description: Optional: what the DAG is for

nodes.description: The steps, 1 to 10, each with a unique name

type.description: 'subtask' runs its instructions as a subtask. 'check' polls its completion_check, and only a 'check' node honors 'tools': every other type ignores them. 'callback' runs AFTER its predecessors and receives their results as context (point a context_flow edge at it); it accepts frame_type / model / timeout_seconds like a subtask. If callbacks are switched off on this server, a callback completes at once without running. 'gate' auto-passes: a marker, not a quality check. 'fix' repairs a failed node (parent_node). 'wait' waits for a Claude Code job, a pull request or a file (wait_for) with no model and no shell, polled every completion_check_interval seconds (a pr wait at most once a minute), until the condition holds (it completes), can no longer hold, or timeout_seconds or max_check_attempts runs out (it fails). A node that only waits for a job, a PR or a file must be a 'wait' node, not a 'check' node. In a DAG created by a background (internal_only) turn, waits and the built-in PR check are the only conditions allowed. A wait node takes name, type, instructions "" and wait_for, and optionally timeout_seconds, completion_check_interval, max_check_attempts and description.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the node may run (the server has a default and a ceiling). A node still running past it is cancelled and failed, so size it to the work. For a 'check' or 'wait' node with max_check_attempts and completion_check_interval, it is raised to cover the polls (a Note line says so), and the DAG is refused when that is above the ceiling.

stall_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds without activity before the node fails; 0 = no stall check. Omitted: the server's default.

completion_check.description: Shell command polled each tick: exit 0 = success, 1 = failed, 2 = still running. For work that ends in a pull request, use the built-in check 'python -m nous.dag.typed_checks pr <owner/repo> --head <branch>' (or --pr <n>) exactly as written, with a completion_check_interval of 300 or more: it passes once that PR exists and fails if it is closed without a merge. If the node launches a Claude Code job (claude-jobs/runner.sh launch) that opens the PR, have it write the job id to a workspace file (redirect runner.sh launch's output) and add ' --job-file <absolute path of that file>' to the same check: the node then fails when the job ends without the PR. Only this exact check, on the node that opens the PR, counts toward your score; a job-status or gh check of your own, or a pr wait on another node, earns nothing. A DAG created by a background (internal_only) turn may carry no other completion_check: use a 'wait' node.

completion_check_interval.description: Seconds between completion check polls, or between a wait node's polls (default: every tick; a pr wait at least 60)

max_check_attempts.description: Max poll attempts (completion check or wait) before node fails

wait_for.description: (type='wait' only) What to wait for. job: {"kind": "job", "job_id": "job-20261027-101500-ab12cd34", "until": "completed"}: a Claude Code job (runner.sh launch prints its id); until "finished" (the default) takes any end, "completed" fails the node if the job ends any other way (a dead process counts as failed). pr: {"kind": "pr", "number": 810, "repo": "owner/name", "until": "merged"}: repo defaults to the server's default repository; until is "merged" (fails if closed without a merge), "closed", "head_changed" (needs "head", the sha it waits to move from), "checks_done" (every check run on the head finished, failed ones named; pending while GitHub lists no check run on the head, so a repository without CI never passes it; with "head", fails if the head moved) or "review_on_head" (a review on the current head, from a login starting with "reviewer" when given). GitHub errors never fail a pr wait; it polls at most once a minute. file: {"kind": "file", "path": "research/out.md", "nonempty": true}: a workspace path with no hidden component (nonempty waits for content, or an entry in a directory).

parent_node.description: (type='fix' only) The node this fix repairs; the fix runs when that node fails. Add an 'on_failure' edge with from_node = that node and to_node = this fix node.

fix_actions.description: (type='fix' only) The actions the fix may take: retry the node as it was or with amended instructions (where amended retries are switched off, it retries as is), skip it and let the DAG go on, or fail it for good.

max_fix_attempts.description: (type='fix' only) Fix attempts per failure of the node. Default 1.

expected_modes.description: (type='fix' only) Failure modes you expect. Not used yet.

edges.description: Links between nodes, by name. Omit for a single node.

edge_type.description: 'dependency' (default): to_node runs after from_node. 'context_flow': the same, and to_node also gets from_node's result. 'on_failure': from a node to its fix node. 'cancel_cascade': to_node does not wait, but is cancelled if from_node fails.

token_budget.description: Optional token budget for the whole DAG; the server may stop it once spent.
